title: Max Area of Island
description:
You are given an `m x n` binary matrix `grid`. An **island** is a group of `1`s (representing land) connected **4-directionally** (horizontally or vertically). Diagonal cells are not connected. You may assume all four edges of the grid are surrounded by water (`0`).

The **area** of an island is the number of cells with a value `1` in that island.

Return the maximum area of an island in `grid`. If there is no island, return `0`.
hints: Whenever you discover an unvisited land cell (`1`), flood-fill its entire connected component using DFS or BFS while counting how many cells you visit.
Mark visited land cells (either by flipping them to `0` or using a separate `visited` matrix) so each cell is counted at most once.
Keep track of the maximum component size seen across the entire grid, initializing the answer to `0` in case there is no land.

examples.explanation: The largest connected component of 1s has area 6 (note that the nearby diagonal cluster is not connected to it).
The grid contains only water (0s), so the maximum island area is 0.
Diagonal 1s are not connected, so there are five separate islands each of area 1.
